players.name: DeMario Douglas
players.waiver_note:
Over his last five games, DeMario Douglas has averaged 70.4 receiving yards and scored four touchdowns. He's had 65 or more receiving yards in four of those five games.

With AJ Brown continuing to miss time with knee and ankle injuries, the 5-8, 185-pound Douglas has stepped up as New England's No. 1 receiver. He gets an appealing Week 10 matchup against a Lions defense that has given up more passing yards than any other team in the league.

players.name: Caleb Douglas
players.waiver_note:
Let us remember the magnificent leaping 20-yard catch that Dolphins rookie Caleb Douglas made in Week 9 and not the egregious drop he had on a fourth down late in the game to snuff out the Dolphins' hopes of a comeback in their 19-9 home loss to the Lions.

That drop aside, Douglas is clearly the Dolphins' best receiver. The third-round pick from Texas Tech is averaging 3.8 catches, 59.2 yards and 0.4 touchdowns per game in a very limited Miami passing attack.

Douglas has a manageable schedule the rest of the way and can be a reasonable third receiver or flex in any given week. It's also possible he's just scratching the surface of his potential and could find a higher gear before the season is out.

players.name: Audric Estime
players.waiver_note:
Saints beat writer and podcaster Nick Underhill is extremely dialed in on the team he covers. He was asked on Twitter last week whether he thought Audric Estime would lead the Saints in touches in Week 9 after the team released Kendre Miller.

"I picked (Estime) up in fantasy on Wednesday," Underhill replied.

Estime did lead the Saints backfield in touches Sunday against the Browns, with 15-72-1 rushing and 1-5-0 receiving. Alvin Kamara out-snapped Estime 37-35, but Kamara had only nine touches.

The 5-11, 227 Estime is a physical north-south runner who can take care of business at the goal line but doesn't offer much in the way of pass catching. The 31-year-old Kamara is still a good pass catcher and a useful contributor, but he can't carry a running game any longer.

The question is when Travis Etienne Jr. will return from a hamstring injury. Etienne hasn't played since Week 3. The Saints still haven't designated him to return from injured reserve, but that could happen soon.

If Etienne were to return this week, Estime's value would be gutted. The Saints paid Etienne handsomely in free agency and wouldn't let him collect dust on the sideline upon his return.

But it seems unlikely that Etienne will be back this week, and the Saints have an attractive running-game matchup against the Panthers. Entering Week 9, only the Saints themselves had given up more fantasy points per game to RBs than the Panthers.

Unless we get word early in the week that Etienne has a good chance to return for Week 10, consider grabbing Estime if you need to patch a hole at running back this week.

players.name: Jakobi Meyers
players.waiver_note:
Jakobi Meyers has 26-374-2 on 37 targets. He hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 3, and only once this season has Meyers amassed more than 65 receiving yards in a game.

But the Jaguars play two of their next three games against the Titans, who have allowed the second-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers. In his two games against Tennessee last season, Meyers had 6-90-1 on six targets and 5-44-0 on six targets.

Meyers is averaging 2.10 yards per route run against man defense this season, according to Fantasy Points Data. In Week 11, Meyers faces the Giants, who play man coverage at the fourth-highest rate in the league.

It doesn't hurt that Meyers is tied to Trevor Lawrence, who's on a roll. Lawrence has thrown for 1,089 yards and 10 touchdowns over his last four games, averaging 9.1 yards per pass attempt.

Meyers should be playable as a WR3 or flex for at least the next three weeks.

players.name: Ryan Flournoy
players.waiver_note:
With Cowboys WR George Pickens scratched in Week 9 due to a hamstring injury, No. 3 WR Ryan Flournoy seemed poised for a good day against a Colts defense that has been getting punked by slot receivers for most of the season.

Flournoy had an early seven-yard catch, then didn't have another reception until he beat Sauce Gardner for a 46-yard gain late in the fourth quarter.

It's unclear whether Pickens will miss additional time, but Flournoy had become fantasy-relevant even with Pickens and CeeDee Lamb both healthy. Before Week 9, Flournoy had either scored a touchdown or produced 70-plus receiving yards in four consecutive games.

Despite his disappointing performance in Week 10, Flournoy will probably be ranked as a top-30 receiver in a neutral Week 10 matchup against the 49ers if Pickens is out. And even if Pickens is back by Week 12, Flournoy will be worth flex consideration that week in a home matchup against an Eagles defense that has been bludgeoned by slot receivers in 2026.

players.name: Tank Dell
players.waiver_note: It was great to see Tank Dell have a 4-105-1 performance in Week 9. The undersized receiver sustained a gruesome injury late in the 2024 season, tearing multiple knee ligaments, dislocating his kneecap and incurring meniscus damage. Dell finally returned in Week 7 and had a 43-yard catch against the Giants. He was more involved in Week 9, playing 53.2% of the Texans' offensive snaps and drawing nine targets. But C.J. Stroud threw for 384 yards and five touchdowns, and there won't be that much goodness to divide among the five receivers the Texans are using every week. As nice a story as the Dell comeback is, adding him to your roster might not pay off.

players.name: Darren Waller
players.waiver_note:
With the Panthers' wide receivers having trouble shaking free from the coverage of the Broncos' cornerbacks in Week 9, Darren Waller stepped up and had his biggest game of the season, with 8-90-1 on a team-high 10 targets. Waller ran routes on 69% of QB Bryce Young's dropbacks.

Seemingly bothered by a toe injury, Waller had only two catches in his previous three games — although one of them went for a 50-yard touchdown. We might have thrown Waller into the Fool's Gold section of this article if not for a favorable Week 10 matchup with the Saints.

Entering Week 9, the Saints had allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game to tight ends. New Orleans has allowed 47-521-5 to TEs in eight games. The Saints had kept Cleveland's Harold Fannin Jr. under wraps for most of their game against the Browns last week until Fannin bounced off some inept Saints tackle attempts to score a late 39-yard touchdown.

Waller is a viable Week 10 streaming option.

players.name: Antonio Williams
players.waiver_note:
Third-round rookie Antonio Williams should be prominently involved in the Washington passing game for the rest of the regular season with Terry McLaurin out for the year with a torn patellar tendon. In the two games since McLaurin's injury, Williams has 8-79-0 on 13 targets.

Williams can play in the slot or outside, although he's been playing the majority of his snaps on the perimeter, with Stefon Diggs serving as the Commanders' primary slot man.

The upcoming schedule is WR-friendly for Washington, with Williams and the Commanders not running into an adverse matchup until they face Minnesota in Week 16.

Williams can be a handy utility tool for fantasy managers in the coming weeks.

players.name: Corey Kiner
players.waiver_note:
Over the summer, fantasy managers tried to figure out how to play a New England backfield that was expected to feature Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. In Week 10, the New England backfield could feature Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.

Stevenson left the Patriots' Week 9 loss to the Packers with a knee injury. As of Sunday, it was unclear what sort of injury Stevenson has and how much time, if any, he might miss. Henderson said last week that he was hospitalized after experiencing neurological symptoms. He did not play on Sunday, and it's unclear when he'll return.

Kiner played only 11 snaps Sunday but had carries on eight of them and ran for 55 yards and his first NFL touchdown. (Larison played more snaps than Kiner but won't be a factor in the running game.) For the season, Kiner has 50-244-1 rushing and 2-16-0 receiving on two targets.

If you're thinking about trying to acquire Kiner, monitor the news on Stevenson and Henderson, and bid on Kiner accordingly.

players.name: Pat Freiermuth
players.waiver_note:
With Colston Loveland and Dallas Goedert on bye in Week 10, some fantasy managers might be in search of a tight end to stream this week. Pat Freiermuth isn't having a banner season but could be a palatable option this week based on matchup.

Freiermuth has been splitting TE targets with Darnell Washington and has an uninspiring 11.7% target share. Although Freiermuth has delivered five touchdowns (including one on a goal-line tush push), he's averaging 4.4 targets, 3.1 catches and 29.4 receiving yards per game.

But Freiermuth has a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Bengals. He had only 2-30-0 on four targets in a Week 6 game against Cincinnati, but Bengals defensive coordinator Al Golden's unit is usually content to give up receptions to tight ends over the middle.

Cincinnati entered Week 9 having allowed the ninth-most fantasy points to tight ends, even though no TE has scored a touchdown against the Bengals. Last year under Golden, the Bengals gave up the most catches, receiving yards and touchdowns to tight ends.

Last week, the Titans' Gunnar Helm had a season-best 5-76-0 day against the Bengals. Helm hadn't produced more than 28 receiving yards in any other game this year.

Despite his humble reception and yardage totals this season, Freiermuth has streaming appeal in Week 9.

players.name: Tyler Higbee
players.waiver_note:
Tyler Higbee had 18-212-1 over a three-game stretch from Week 3 to Week 5. Since then, he's had 22 or fewer receiving yards in four consecutive games.

Despite the downturn, this might be a good time to buy in on Higbee. WR Davante Adams is expected to be out for at least another 5-6 weeks with a severe hamstring injury. WR Puka Nacua sustained a knee injury of unknown severity on Sunday. TE Terrance Ferguson was on his way back from an ankle injury when he picked up a hamstring injury in practice last week.

Head coach Sean McVay has leaned aggressively into multiple-TE sets the last two seasons and may have to do so out of necessity in the weeks to come.

Higbee led the Rams' tight ends in snaps (60), routes (35) and targets (5) in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders, although his five targets netted only a single 13-yard catch.

Still, Higbee has a promising target outlook this week against an Arizona defense that has allowed the eighth-most fantasy points to tight ends.

players.name: Dylan Sampson
players.waiver_note: Dylan Sampson will be regarded as a worthy waiver target in some quarters. He will not be regarded as such here. Yes, Sampson has played more than half of the Browns' offensive snaps since returning from a knee injury in Week 7. Yes, he is kneecapping the fantasy value of Browns RB Quinshon Judkins. But Sampson is not a credible threat as a runner. His eight carries against the Saints on Sunday were a season high. He has 12 catches for 121 yards over his last three games, but some of that was pure garbage-time production. Sampson has averaged 3.1 yards per carry over 19 NFL games and is still looking for his first rushing touchdown. (He has two TD catches.) Sampson is no threat to Judkins' early-down role and doesn't offer enough passing-game production to be startable. He is not worth your FAAB money unless Judkins gets hurt.

players.name: Jordan Watkins
players.waiver_note:
Depleted by injuries at wide receiver, the 49ers gave second-year WR Jordan Watkins an 83.6% target share Sunday against the Raiders, and he responded with 4-86-1 on four targets.

Mike Evans missed Week 9 with Achilles tendinitis in his foot, and Deebo Samuel was out with a hamstring. It's possible one or both could be back this week.

If not, Watkins could be QB Brock Purdy's lead receiver against a Swiss cheese Cowboys defense that had allowed the sixth-most fantasy points to wide receivers entering Week 6. Even if one of Evans or Samuel is back, Watkins could be at least flex-worthy in such a favorable matchup.

But Watkins is probably just a one-week rental, since Evans figures to be back by Week 11 at the latest, and the 49ers have difficult matchups in Weeks 11 and 12 against the Vikings and Seahawks, respectively.

players.name: Xavier Hutchinson
players.waiver_note:
The Texans are using an unwieldy five-man receiver rotation that includes Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Marvin Harrison Jr., Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte.

Collins is rostered everywhere, as he should be. Marvin Harrison Jr. is rostered in 64% of Yahoo leagues. Houston's other three receivers are rostered in less than half of Yahoo leagues. We don't think Dell or Boutte are worth picking up, but Hutchison is intriguing.

Hutchinson led Houston's receivers in snaps (57) and routes (34) Sunday vs. the Chargers. He had 3-29-1 on five targets. Hutchinson has scored a touchdown in two straight games. He's had three or more catches in all but one of his eight games this season.

What's significant here is that Hutchinson is now serving as the Texans' primary slot receiver. Hutchinson also has favorable matchups the next two weeks. Entering Week 9, the Browns had allowed the 11th-most fantasy points per game to slot receivers, and the Colts had allowed the fifth-most.

It should be easy to sneak Hutchinson through with a $1 or $0 FAAB bid since he was overshadowed by a couple of his teammates in Week 9.

players.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
players.waiver_note:
Frequently listed as a stash candidate in this article, Chris Rodriguez Jr. is getting a full listing this week because the Jaguars' lead RB, Bhayshul Tuten, has been dealing with foot and ankle injuries.

Tuten played against the Ravens last Thursday night but was limited to a 36% snap share. He had 12-29-0 rushing and no receptions. Rodriguez played five more snaps than Tuten and had 10-19-1 rushing and 2-13-0 receiving.

Rodriguez hasn't carried the ball more than 11 times in any game this season, and his two catches last week doubled his reception total for 2026. Rodriguez is a classic between-the-tackles grinder. He has 55 carries for 228 yards this season, but he's already punched in four touchdowns.

Tuten's questionable health makes Rodriguez an interesting speculative add, especially with some favorable matchups ahead. Two of the Jaguars' next three games are against the Titans, who rank 27th in defense-adjusted value over average (DVOA) vs. the run. In Week 11, the Jaguars face the Giants, who rank 20th in DVOA vs. the run.

players.name: Emmett Johnson
players.waiver_note: Chiefs rookie Emmett Johnson continues to look good in limited action behind workhorse Kenneth Walker III. If Walker were to go down, Johnson would become fantasy gold.

players.name: Kaelon Black
players.waiver_note:
At 7-1, the 49ers are well positioned for the playoffs. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has long talked about managing RB Christian McCaffrey's workload more judiciously but often can't seem to help himself when it comes to limiting CMC's touches.

Rookie RB Kaelon Black is giving Shanahan a reason to limit McCaffrey's usage as the playoffs draw closer. A third-round pick out of Indiana, Black has 68-303-1 rushing for an average of 4.5 yards per carry. He's well above league average in rushing success rate and well below league average in stuff rate.

Last week against the Raiders, Black had 11-70-0 rushing in a 38-17 win over the Raiders. He could get double-digit carries against another poor defense this week when the 49ers visit the Cowboys.

Black is now an essential handcuff if you're a McCaffrey stakeholder. Even if you aren't rostering CMC, Black is worth rostering, because a McCaffrey injury would send Black's fantasy value to the moon.

players.name: Kayshon Boutte
players.waiver_note: Kayshon Boutte had a big game Sunday, with 4-125-2 on five targets. Resist the urge to chase last week's fantasy points. The Texans have a messy five-man WR rotation, and Boutte had the lowest snap share among the five receivers Houston used in Week 9, playing 37.1% of the offensive snaps. Boutte is a big-play artist, but the limited usage won't give him enough opportunities to make big plays consistently.

players.name: Konata Mumpfield
players.waiver_note:
WR Puka Nacua sustained a knee injury on the Rams' final offensive play of their 20-13 win over the Commanders in Week 9. We were still awaiting more details on the Nacua injury when this article was published Monday morning. Rams WR Davante Adams is expected to be out until late in the regular season with a severe hamstring injury.

Second-year receiver Konata Mumpfield could be the Rams' No. 1 receiver by default this week against the Cardinals — and perhaps when the Rams emerge from their Week 11 bye if the Nacua injury turns out to be significant.

Mumpfield played two fewer snaps and had three fewer targets than Rams WR Tutu Atwell on Sunday, but Atwell has demonstrated over his five-plus NFL seasons that he has little to offer fantasy managers.

A protege of Adams, Mumpfield has flashed at times over 26 NFL games. He has 11-162-1 this season on 23 targets,

It's possible no Rams receiver provides satisfying fantasy value while Nacua is out, but Mumpfield probably has the best chance to deliver some.

players.name: Seth McGowan
players.waiver_note:
The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, and there's a good chance the Colts will move RB Jonathan Taylor before the deadline. Taylor seemed to be bidding adieu after the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys when he offered thanks to the city of Indianapolis while being interviewed at his locker.

If indeed Taylor is traded, seventh-round rookie Seth McGowan becomes the Colts' new lead back. McGowan has performed well in a backup role to this point, with 43-208-1 rushing for an average of 4.8 yards per carry. He scored his first touchdown of the season on Sunday after Taylor lost his shoe on a run to the Cowboys' 2-yard line. McGowan came in and scored on the next play.

McGowan has only 5-9-0 receiving, but he showed some pass-catching aptitude over three college seasons at Oklahoma, New Mexico State and Kentucky.

The 6-0, 223-pound McGowan has a nice combination of size and speed. He ran a 4.49 at this year's scouting combine and also had a 42 1/2-inch vertical jump.

The pessimistic view is that the Colts' offense could be a sinkhole if they trade Taylor. QB Daniel Jones and WR Josh Downs have been involved in trade rumors as well.

But lead RBs are usually hard to find nine weeks into the regular season, and McGowan instantly becomes a startable fantasy asset if the Colts trade away Taylor.

players.name: Bam Knight
players.waiver_note:
There's no guarantee Bam Knight will be able to return from the concussion that sidelined him in Week 9, but if Knight comes back this week, he might get a majority of the rushing load against the Rams.

Cardinals rookie Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss a few weeks with an ankle injury. With Knight out in Week 9, Tyler Allgeier dominated backfield touches for the Cardinals in a 17-3 loss to the Seahawks, with 17-46-0 rushing and 2-0-0 receiving.

Knight has been a more effective runner than Allgeier, albeit over a small sample size. Knight is averaging 6.0 yards per carry on 28 carries. Allgeier is averaging 4.1 yards per carry. Allgeier ripped apart the Dallas defense after Knight left with a concussion, but Allgeier hasn't been particularly effective this season otherwise.

The Cardinals have tough matchups against the Rams and Chiefs the next two weeks, but Knight could be worth a speculative addition.

players.name: Darnell Washington
players.waiver_note:
If you're going to stream a Pittsburgh tight end this week in a favorable matchup against the Bengals, we would prefer Pat Freiermuth, but he may already be rostered in your league. Darnell Washington is rostered in only 3% of Yahoo leagues, even though his receiving numbers are similar to Freiermuth's

Freiermuth has 25-235-4 on 35 targets. Washington has 19-254-3 on 28 targets. Washington has been ultra-efficient this season, averaging 9.4 yards per target and 2.23 yards per route run while scoring a touchdown on 10.7% of his targets.

For more information on what makes Washington's matchup with Cincinnati so appealing, see the report on Freiermuth above. In the Steelers' Week 3 game against the Bengals, Washington had 3-67-0 on four targets.

Deeper leagues sometimes have limited streaming options at tight end, but Washington looks like a good one for Week 10.

players.name: Kaleb Johnson
players.waiver_note: Kaleb Johnson had 14-68-1 rushing for the Packers Sunday after Josh Jacobs left with a finger injury. Johnson gained half his yardage on one run. The Packers have been ineffective running the ball all season. Their offensive line ranks last in the run-blocking metric adjusted line yards by a wide margin. If Jacobs is out next week, Johnson will share work with Pierre Strong Jr., and there's at least a small chance MarShawn Lloyd could be back from the knee injury that kept him out of Week 9. Do not pursue Johnson.

players.name: Mike Washington Jr.
players.waiver_note:
A popular waiver addition after getting 25 carries in Week 8, Mike Washington Jr. remains available in 51% of Yahoo leagues but will be less sought after following a poor game against a good San Francisco run defense.

Washington carried six times against the 49ers Sunday for -3 yards. He was not targeted in the passing game.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak turned back to Ashton Jeanty as his primary running back in Week 9. Jeanty out-snapped Washington 32-17. They both had six carries, but unlike Washington, Jeanty was active in the passing game, with seven targets and five catches (for -5 yards).

For now, Washington is nothing more than a depth piece for fantasy. He's not startable this week in a difficult matchup against the Seahawks.

players.name: Samaje Perine
players.waiver_note: Samaje Perine had 11 carries in Week 9, which was two more than starter Chase Brown, although seven of Perine's 11 carries came in the Bengals' final two drives of the game, when they were killing clock in a 17-point win over the Falcons. Perine has no stand-alone value, but the Cincinnati offense is humming, so Perine has become a priority handcuff for Brown stakeholders.

players.name: Van Jefferson
players.waiver_note: Injuries to Terry McLaurin, Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown moved Van Jefferson up the Commanders' WR depth chart in Week 9, and he had 5-58-1 on seven targets vs. the Rams. McLaurin is out for the season, and Brown is on IR, but Burks' foot injury isn't believed to be long-term. Even if it were, Jefferson would not be worth adding.

players.name: Terrance Ferguson
players.waiver_note: In a tale from the "I hate fantasy football" files, Terrance Ferguson seemed set to return from a high-ankle sprain in Week 9 but injured his hamstring in practice and now seems likely to miss several more weeks. Fantasy managers with an available roster spot and TE woes might want to consider picking up Ferguson for a buck and stashing him. If he returns before WR Davante Adams is back from his hamstring injury sometime in December, Ferguson could eventually be a high-volume target earner. None of the Rams' other tight ends have been able to provide consistent fantasy value.
